questions.question: A train 380 m long passes a pole in 38 seconds. How long will it take to pass a bridge 920 m long?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time to cross a **pole** (T₁) ∝ Length of **train** (LT)

Time to cross a **bridge** (T₂) ∝ (Length of **train** + Length of **bridge**)

T₂ = 38 × (380 + 920) ÷ 380

T₂ = 38 × 1300 ÷ 380 = 130 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 130 sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **train** (LT) = 380 m

Time to pass the **pole** (t₁) = 38 sec

Length of **bridge** (LB) = 920 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total Distance when crossing a bridge = LT + LB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26a6ca9b2603be8f13a39905d5ab5c6b877de25ae46bdcd64d2d7d0e04d136b8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of train = Length of train ÷ Time taken to cross pole

⇒ Speed = 380 ÷ 38 = 10 m/sec

⇒ Total distance to cross bridge = 380 + 920 = 1300 m

⇒ Time taken = Total distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 1300 ÷ 10 = 130 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 130 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a **pole** or a **standing man**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train**.

Crossing Long Objects

When a train crosses a **bridge**, **platform**, or **tunnel**, the distance covered is the sum of the **length of the train** and the **object**.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/sec**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/sec** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the side length of two cubes is 4 : 3. If the difference in the surface area of the two cubes is 42 m², then find the combined volume for both cubes. (m ³)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **sides** = 4 : 3

Ratio of **surface areas** = 4² : 3² = 16 : 9

Difference in area parts = 16 − 9 = 7 units → 42 m² ∴ 1 unit = 6 m²

Actual side lengths **a₁** and **a₂**: 6×a² = Area ⇒ 6×(4x)² − 6×(3x)² = 42 ⇒ 6×x²(16 − 9) = 42 ⇒ x = 1 m

Combined Volume = 4³ + 3³ = 64 + 27 = 91 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 91 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **side lengths** = 4 : 3, Difference in **Total Surface Area** = 42 m².

**Formula Used:** Total Surface Area of Cube = 6a²; Volume of Cube = a³.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84b5cede102873c8a4d72930e327e89f1395fa6a99aa76fcb7f2a37d651c10d6.png] 

⇒ Let sides be 4x and 3x.

⇒ Surface Area 1 = 6 × (4x)² = 96x²

⇒ Surface Area 2 = 6 × (3x)² = 54x²

⇒ Difference = 96x² − 54x² = 42

⇒ 42x² = 42 ⇒ x² = 1 ⇒ x = 1 m

⇒ Side 1 = 4 m, Side 2 = 3 m

⇒ Combined Volume = (4)³ + (3)³

⇒ Combined Volume = 64 + 27 = 91 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 91 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube Properties

Lateral Surface Area = 4a². Diagonal of a cube = a√3. It has 12 edges and 8 vertices.

Ratio Relationship

If side ratio is x:y, then Area ratio is x²:y² and Volume ratio is x³:y³.</p

questions.question: The ratio of radii of a cylinder to a that of a cone is 1 : 2. if their heights are equal, find the ratio of their volumes
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Volume of Cylinder** (V꜀y) to **Volume of Cone** (V꜀ₒ) is given by πr₁²h : (1/3)πr₂²h.

Since **heights** are equal, ratio is r₁² : (1/3)r₂².

Given **radius ratio** r₁ : r₂ = 1 : 2.

Ratio = 1² : (1/3)×2² = 1 : 4/3 = 3 : 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Radii** (r₁ : r₂) = 1 : 2

Ratio of **Heights** (h₁ : h₂) = 1 : 1

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Cylinder** = πr²h

Volume of **Cone** = (1/3)πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/832acbcf9f7658e4407f7ba2ee6289430061f13fdb3648010098125829a1d66b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let radius of **Cylinder** = x and radius of **Cone** = 2x.

⇒ Let the height of both be h.

⇒ Volume of **Cylinder** (V₁) = π × (x)² × h = πx²h

⇒ Volume of **Cone** (V₂) = (1/3) × π × (2x)² × h = (4/3)πx²h

⇒ Ratio = V₁ : V₂ = πx²h : (4/3)πx²h

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 4/3

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Three-Dimensional Shapes

If a **Cylinder** and a **Cone** have the same radius and height, the volume of the cylinder is exactly 3 times the volume of the cone.

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area of a **Cylinder** is given by 2πr(h + r), including both the curved surface and the two circular bases.

Slant Height of Cone

For a **Cone**, the slant height l is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: l = √(r² + h²).</p

questions.question: What is the angle of depression of the sun when the shadow of a pole of height x m is (x)/({sqrt 3 )}m?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the **height** of the **pole** to the **length** of its **shadow** is given by x : (x / √3).

Simplified ratio = 1 : (1 / √3) = √3 : 1.

For a **right-angled triangle**, if the ratio of **Perpendicular** to **Base** is √3 : 1, then the **angle of elevation** (θ) is 60°.

The **angle of depression** of the sun is equal to the **angle of elevation** of the sun from the ground.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height** of the **pole** (AB) = x m

**Length** of the **shadow** (BC) = x / √3 m

**Formula Used:**

In a **right-angled triangle**, tan θ = **Perpendicular** / **Base**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40d36efaa4e5ac5618e6b56ffb6ceb10df7f9d9560916061248116cab55e958e.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let θ be the **angle of elevation** of the sun.

⇒ tan θ = AB / BC

⇒ tan θ = x / (x / √3)

⇒ tan θ = x × (√3 / x)

⇒ tan θ = √3

We know that tan 60° = √3

⇒ θ = 60°

Since the **angle of depression** is equal to the **angle of elevation** (alternate interior angles), the required angle is 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression and Elevation

The **angle of elevation** and **angle of depression** are always equal for a given pair of points because they are **alternate interior angles** formed by a transversal cutting two horizontal parallel lines.

Standard Trigonometric Ratios (tan)

Key values include: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3. These ratios define the relation between **height** and **distance**.

Relationship Rule

If **Height** > **Shadow**, the angle is greater than 45°. If **Height** < **Shadow**, the angle is less than 45°. If they are equal, the angle is exactly 45°.</p

questions.question: The average age of A, B and C, 5 years ago, was 21 years. The average age of B and C 3 years from now will be 25.5 years. What is the present age (in years) of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present **Average Age** of **A, B and C** = 21 + 5 = 26 years

Present **Average Age** of **B and C** = 25.5 − 3 = 22.5 years

Present **Age** of **A** = (Total of A, B, C) − (Total of B, C)

Present **Age** of **A** = (26 × 3) − (22.5 × 2) = 78 − 45 = 33 years

**∴ The correct answer is 33 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of **A, B, C** (5 years ago) = 21 years

Average age of **B, C** (3 years hence) = 25.5 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of Persons

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6197841ade49cb6df24b17c4b5d9a705e28890f58b9e1daa68fba5f16d7780be.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ages of **A, B, C** (5 years ago) = 21 × 3 = 63 years

⇒ Present Sum of ages of **A, B, C** = 63 + (3 × 5) = 78 years

⇒ Sum of ages of **B and C** (3 years from now) = 25.5 × 2 = 51 years

⇒ Present Sum of ages of **B and C** = 51 − (2 × 3) = 51 − 6 = 45 years

⇒ Present age of **A** = (Present Sum of A, B, C) − (Present Sum of B, C)

⇒ Present age of **A** = 78 − 45 = 33 years

**∴ The correct answer is 33 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Age Property

If the age of each person in a group increases or decreases by **n** years, the **Average Age** of the group also increases or decreases by **n** years.

Sum and Average Relation

The sum of ages of **n** people after **t** years = (Present Sum) + (n × t).

Finding Individual Value

To find the age of a specific person from a group, subtract the sum of the ages of the remaining members from the total sum: **A = Sum(All) − Sum(Others)**.</p

questions.question: Ram can row downstream 20 km in 2 hours, and the upstream 4 km in 2 hours. What will be the speed of rowing in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Downstream Speed (D)** = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 km/hr

**Upstream Speed (U)** = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 km/hr

**Still Water Speed** = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (10 + 2) ÷ 2 = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Downstream distance = 20 km, Time = 2 hrs; Upstream distance = 4 km, Time = 2 hrs.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Still water speed (u) = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f19f1d6f692541253fb7305c68ac8dd9bafc7af61aac6a7d7371e9a48c6ba06b.png] 

⇒ Downstream Speed (u + v) = 20 / 2 = 10 km/hr

⇒ Upstream Speed (u − v) = 4 / 2 = 2 km/hr

⇒ Adding both equations: (u + v) + (u − v) = 10 + 2

⇒ 2u = 12

⇒ u = 12 / 2 = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Stream Speed Formula

The speed of the stream or current (v) is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: v = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream speed = Speed in still water + Speed of stream. Upstream speed = Speed in still water − Speed of stream.</p

questions.question: If x + y = 15, xy = 14 then find the value of x - y.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify two **factors** of 14 such that their **sum** is 15.

Factors of 14 are 14 and 1 (since 14 × 1 = 14 and 14 + 1 = 15).

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

x + y = 15

xy = 14

(x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

⇒ (x − y)² = 225 − 56

⇒ (x − y)² = 169

⇒ x − y = √169

⇒ x − y = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum and Difference

(x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy. This identity relates the sum, difference, and product of two numbers.

Square of a Binomial

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy and (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy.

Difference of Squares

x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y). This is used when the sum and difference are known to find the difference of their squares.</p

questions.question: Rs. 9,500 is divided among three friends A, B and C such that B gets 75% of the amount that A gets and the ratio between A and C's shares is 8 ∶ 5. The amount (in Rs.) that B gets is:

Ratio of **A : C** = 8 : 5 and **B** gets 75% of **A**.

If **A** = 8 units, then **B** = 75% of 8 = 6 units.

Ratio **A : B : C** = 8 : 6 : 5. Total units = 8 + 6 + 5 = 19 units.

19 units = ₹9,500 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹500.

**B** share = 6 × 500 = ₹3,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

⇒ 19x = 9500

⇒ x = 9500 ÷ 19 = 500.

⇒ **B** share = 6x = 6 × 500 = 3000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

questions.question: Person A work 20% more than person B. Total works list is 110. Then what is work of B?

questions.question: Two circles with centres O and P and radii 17 cm and 10 cm, respectively, intersect each other at A and B. The length of the common chord AB is 16 cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle OAP (in cm)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **common chord** AB is bisected by the line of centres OP at M, so AM = 8 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplets** for right-angled triangles ΔAMO and ΔAMP:

For ΔAMO (hypotenuse 17, leg 8): OM = √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm.

For ΔAMP (hypotenuse 10, leg 8): PM = √(10² − 8²) = 6 cm.

Distance between centres OP = OM + PM = 15 + 6 = 21 cm.

Perimeter of ΔOAP = OA + AP + OP = 17 + 10 + 21 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle (centre O), OA = 17 cm

Radius of second circle (centre P), PA = 10 cm

Length of **common chord**, AB = 16 cm

**Formula Used:**

The line joining the centres of two intersecting circles is the **perpendicular bisector** of their common chord.

**Pythagoras Theorem:** Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

Perimeter of triangle = Sum of all three sides

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/826178678a41af1ac856d119e6f9dd69f022f769c43bbe26bea14b00b5658229.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the line joining the centres O and P intersect the common chord AB at point M.

⇒ AM = MB = AB ÷ 2

⇒ AM = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

Since OP is perpendicular to AB, ΔAMO and ΔAMP are **right-angled triangles** at M.

In right-angled ΔAMO, using Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 17² = OM² + 8²

⇒ 289 = OM² + 64

⇒ OM² = 289 − 64 = 225

⇒ OM = √225 = 15 cm

In right-angled ΔAMP, using Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ PA² = PM² + AM²

⇒ 10² = PM² + 8²

⇒ 100 = PM² + 64

⇒ PM² = 100 − 64 = 36

⇒ PM = √36 = 6 cm

Now, the distance between the centres OP is:

⇒ OP = OM + PM

⇒ OP = 15 + 6 = 21 cm

We need to find the **perimeter** of ΔOAP:

⇒ Perimeter of ΔOAP = OA + AP + OP

⇒ Perimeter of ΔOAP = 17 + 10 + 21 = 48 cm

**Why other options are incorrect:**

⇒ **Option (1) 40 cm:** This value does not correspond to any valid geometric configuration of the given circles.

⇒ **Option (3) 25 cm:** This is incorrect as the sum of the two radii alone is 17 + 10 = 27 cm, so the perimeter of the triangle must be greater than 27 cm (since OP > 0).

⇒ **Option (4) 33 cm:** This does not match either of the mathematically possible perimeters (48 cm or 36 cm) derived from the circle properties.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

The line segment connecting the centres of two intersecting circles is always the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

Alternative Case (Centres on Same Side)

If the centres of the circles lie on the same side of the common chord, the distance between the centres is OP = OM − PM = 15 − 6 = 9 cm. In this case, the perimeter of ΔOAP would be 17 + 10 + 9 = 36 cm.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common integer right-triangle side sets like (8, 15, 17) and (6, 8, 10) help solve competitive exam geometry questions extremely quickly without full calculation.</p

questions.question: Any amount becomes Rs. 660 in 5 years and Rs. 776 in 8 years by simple interest. Rate of interest per annum is equal to
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 3 years (8 − 5) = 776 − 660 = ₹116.

Interest for 1 year = 116/3.

**Principal** (P) = 660 − (5 × 116/3) = (1980 − 580) ÷ 3 = 1400/3.

**Rate** (R) = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100 = (116/3 ÷ 1400/3) × 100 = 116/14 = 8(2/7)%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8(2/7)%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** after 5 years (A₅) = ₹660

**Amount** after 8 years (A₈) = ₹776

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8b1341714df194ada6efff99d7009457778f1ebcd1e479c82a4f46cf1c3f968.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 3 years = 776 − 660 = ₹116

⇒ SI for 1 year = 116 ÷ 3

⇒ SI for 5 years = (116 ÷ 3) × 5 = 580 ÷ 3

⇒ **Principal** (P) = A₅ − SI for 5 years

⇒ P = 660 − (580/3) = (1980 − 580) ÷ 3 = 1400/3

⇒ **Rate** (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = ((116/3) × 100) ÷ (1400/3)

⇒ R = (116 × 100) ÷ 1400 = 116 ÷ 14

⇒ R = 58/7 = 8(2/7)%

**∴ The correct answer is 8(2/7)%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Difference in Amounts

In simple interest, the difference between any two amounts is the interest for the difference in years: A₂ − A₁ = P × R × (T₂ − T₁) ÷ 100.

Relationship between P, A and SI

The amount is always the sum of principal and interest: A = P + SI. To find P, subtract total interest from the given amount.

questions.question:
For the given figure, ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with AB as the diameter of the circle. If ∠ADC = 2∠CBA, then find the value of ∠CAB.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4e0c91e0324d1f1b160f45ce903dc6ef5ac8797dcd6c217f76ac133fcbf7117.png]
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°.

∠ADC + ∠CBA = 180°

Given, ∠ADC = 2∠CBA ⇒ 2∠CBA + ∠CBA = 180° ⇒ 3∠CBA = 180° ⇒ ∠CBA = 60°.

Since AB is the diameter, the angle in a semicircle is a right angle: ∠ACB = 90°.

In ΔABC, ∠CAB = 180° − (∠ACB + ∠CBA) = 180° − (90° + 60°) = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

AB is the diameter of the circle.

∠ADC = 2∠CBA

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66bbfc57ec4a829d0967134b6bba827344e3f91d3de52913ce3afd75607d4cc4.png] 

**Theorem Used:**

1. The sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

2. The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is 90° (angle in a semicircle).

3. The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

**Calculations:**

Let ∠CBA = x

⇒ ∠ADC = 2x

Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral:

⇒ ∠ADC + ∠CBA = 180°

⇒ 2x + x = 180°

⇒ 3x = 180°

⇒ x = 60°

⇒ ∠CBA = 60°

Since AB is the diameter of the circle:

⇒ ∠ACB = 90°

Now, in ΔABC:

⇒ ∠CAB + ∠ACB + ∠CBA = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB + 90° + 60° = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB + 150° = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Properties

A quadrilateral is cyclic if all its four vertices lie on a single circle. The sum of opposite angles is always 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°).

Angle in a Semicircle

An angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°).

Exterior Angle of a Cyclic Quadrilateral

The exterior angle formed by extending one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.</p

• **About the Pulitzer Prize:**

 
 
• The Pulitzer Prize was established in **1917** by provisions in the will of **Joseph Pulitzer**, a Hungarian-American journalist and newspaper publisher.
 
• It is administered by **Columbia University** in New York City and recognizes achievements in **journalism, literature, and musical composition**.
 
• The Fiction category specifically honors works of fiction by American authors, published in the preceding calendar year.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for the Pulitzer Prize in Fiction:**
 
 
• The work must be an original piece of fiction written by an **American author**.
 
• It should exhibit **excellence in prose**, character development, and thematic depth.
 
• Preference is given to works that deal with **American life and culture**.
 
 
 
• **Notable Past Winners:**
 
 
• **2020:** "The Nickel Boys" by Colson Whitehead - A novel addressing racism and injustice in a reform school.
 
• **2015:** "All the Light We Cannot See" by Anthony Doerr - A story set during World War II about a blind French girl and a German boy.
 
• **2007:** "The Road" by Cormac McCarthy - A post-apocalyptic tale of a father and son’s journey.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Winning the Pulitzer Prize:**
 
 
• Winning the Pulitzer elevates the author's visibility and critical acclaim.
 
• The prize often leads to increased book sales and wider readership.
 
• It is considered one of the most prestigious awards in American literature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nomination and Selection Process:**

 
 
• Entries are submitted by publishers, and a jury of distinguished writers and critics evaluates the submissions.
 
• The jury selects finalists and sends their recommendations to the Pulitzer Prize Board, which makes the final decision.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility:**
 
 
• To be eligible, the work must be published in the United States during the award year.
 
• The author must be an American citizen.
 
 
 
• **Other Categories of Pulitzer Prizes:**
 
 
• **Journalism:** Includes awards for investigative reporting, public service, and feature writing.
 
• **Music:** Recognizes distinguished compositions by American composers.
 
• **Drama:** Honors plays that depict American life.

questions.question: The National Florence Nightingale Awards, conferred by the President of India in May 2025, are given to which of the following?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Florence Nightingale Awards** are prestigious awards conferred by the **President of India** to honor excellence in the field of **nursing services**. This recognition was established to commemorate the contributions of **Florence Nightingale**, known as the "Lady with the Lamp" and the founder of modern nursing.
 
• The awards are presented annually on **International Nurses Day (May 12)**, which marks the birth anniversary of Florence Nightingale. These awards aim to acknowledge the exemplary work done by **nursing professionals** in public health and patient care.
 
• The recipients of these awards include **nurses** working in various sectors like government hospitals, private healthcare facilities, community health, and other healthcare institutions across India.
 
• The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare plays a pivotal role in organizing the awards. The selection process involves a rigorous evaluation of nominations sent by state governments, union territories, and institutions based on the **nurses' contributions and dedication** to healthcare.
 
• The awards include a **medal, a certificate, and a monetary award** as a token of appreciation for their invaluable services to society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Florence Nightingale:**

 
 
• Florence Nightingale (1820–1910) was an English social reformer and founder of modern nursing. She gained prominence during the **Crimean War** (1853–1856) for her work in improving sanitation and reducing mortality rates in war hospitals.
 
• Her efforts revolutionized healthcare practices and established nursing as a professional career.
 
• The **Florence Nightingale Pledge**, often recited by nurses, emphasizes dedication, ethics, and compassion in nursing practice.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nursing Professionals:**
 
 
• **Nurses** form the backbone of the healthcare system by delivering direct patient care, assisting in surgeries, and managing critical care units.
 
• They play a crucial role in promoting public health initiatives, such as immunization drives, maternal and child health programs, and disease prevention campaigns.
 
• During the **COVID-19 pandemic**, nurses worldwide demonstrated extraordinary courage and resilience in combating the crisis, often working under challenging conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Healthcare Awards in India:**
 
 
• The **Padma Awards** (Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan) also recognize individuals for their exceptional contributions to **medicine and healthcare**.
 
• The **Dr. B.C. Roy National Award** is another prominent recognition given to doctors for their excellence in the field of medicine.
 
• The **Ayushman Bharat Health Awards** are conferred to healthcare professionals and institutions contributing to the success of the **Ayushman Bharat Scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Indian Nursing Council** (INC), established in **1947**, regulates nursing education and practices in India, ensuring quality standards are maintained.
 
• India faces a challenge in terms of the **nurse-to-patient ratio**, which is below the World Health Organization's recommended standards of 1 nurse per 300 patients.
 
• Efforts are being made by the government to improve nursing education and infrastructure through initiatives like the **Skill India Mission** and the establishment of new nursing colleges across the country.

questions.question: According to Union Budget 2025–26, which mission was launched to document and conserve India’s manuscript heritage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Gyan Bharatam Mission**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gyan Bharatam Mission **was launched under the Union Budget 2025–26 to preserve and document **India’s manuscript heritage**, which spans centuries and contains invaluable knowledge.
 
• This mission aims to safeguard ancient manuscripts and texts that are historically and culturally significant, ensuring that they remain accessible to future generations.
 
• India is home to approximately **5 million manuscripts**, considered one of the richest repositories of manuscript heritage globally.
 
• Through this initiative, the government plans to set up a **centralized digital archive** to catalog and digitize manuscripts, thereby protecting them from physical decay or loss.
 
• The mission will also focus on **training archivists** and manuscript conservationists, encouraging research, and promoting awareness about the importance of preserving India’s literary heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manuscript Heritage in India:**

 
 
• India’s manuscripts include works in languages such as **Sanskrit, Prakrit, Tamil, Persian, Arabic, and Urdu**, among others.
 
• The manuscripts cover diverse fields like **philosophy, literature, science, mathematics, medicine, astronomy, and art**.
 
• Important manuscript collections are housed in institutions like the **National Archives of India** and the **Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Conservation:**
 
 
• Many manuscripts are stored in **improper conditions**, leading to their physical deterioration due to humidity, pests, and handling.
 
• The lack of **trained conservators** and inadequate funding for preservation efforts are major hurdles.
 
• Digitization is a key solution to ensure the long-term accessibility and safety of these texts.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Heritage Preservation:**
 
 
• The **National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM)**, launched in 2003, is a government initiative to document and conserve manuscripts.
 
• Under NMM, manuscripts have been digitized and cataloged to prevent their loss.
 
• The **Granth Sanrakshan Abhiyan** complements such efforts by focusing on comprehensive conservation and awareness.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Manuscript Preservation:**
 
 
• Preserving manuscripts helps in understanding India’s **ancient knowledge systems** and cultural history.
 
• It aids scholars and researchers in exploring **historical, scientific, and philosophical advancements** documented in these texts.
 
• Manuscripts serve as a bridge connecting modern society with **ancestral wisdom**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Granth Sanrakshan Abhiyan** emphasizes collaboration with **academic institutions**, libraries, and cultural organizations to maximize the impact of manuscript conservation efforts.
 
• The initiative also aims to create **public awareness campaigns** to highlight the importance of preserving India’s rich literary heritage.
 
• Private collectors and regional archives are encouraged to contribute to the national repository under this mission.
 
• Technology plays a pivotal role in digitization, with advanced tools used for **high-resolution scanning** and metadata creation.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment provided for the setting up of Administrative Tribunals in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**42**__**ⁿd**__** Amendment.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points:__**

 
• The** 42ⁿd constitutional amendment **act of 1976 provided for the setting up of** Administrative Tribunals in India.**

 
 
• The original constitution did not contain any provisions with respect to tribunals.
 
• The 42ⁿd constitutional amendment added a new part **XIV-A and article 323 A** to the Indian constitution.
 
• Article 323 A empowers the parliament to provide for the establishment of administrative tribunals.
 
• Administrative Tribunals adjudicate the disputes and complaints relating to the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to the public service and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union and the States.
 
• The chairman of the central administrative tribunal shall be a **sitting or retired judge of a high court.**
 
• The chairman, vice-chairman, and the members of the central administrative tribunals are appointed by the **President.**
 
• Justice Ranjit Vasantrao More is the current chairman of the central administrative tribunal.
 
 
 
• **The 24th constitutional amendment **of the Indian constitution made it compulsory for the president to give his assent to a constitutional amendment bill.
 
• **The 44th constitutional amendment** of the Indian constitution deleted the right to property from the list of fundamental rights.
 
• **The 59th constitutional amendment **of the Indian constitution empowered the central government to impose an emergency in Punjab when deemed necessary.

__
 
• John Marshall was the first researcher to use the term, ‘Indus Valley Civilization’.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization spread from the year **2500 – 1750 BC** according to radio-carbon dating.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization is **Bronze Age Civilization**__.
 
• The most distinctive feature of the Harappan Civilization was its urbanization.
 
• Moreover, sheep and goats, dogs, humped cattle buffalo, and elephants were domesticated in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The capital cities are Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Some important features of architectures in the Indus Valley Civilization :

__
 
• Urban Cities - Remarkable town planning, and an excellent system of drainage and sanitation.
 
• Large cities divided into two parts-The ‘Citadel’ mound built on the high podium of mud-brick to the west. The town to the east was the main hub of the residential area, which was also surrounded by a massive brick wall.
 
• Streets-Fine drainage system, Well-arranged water supply system, The street lights system, Watch and ward arrangement during the night to oust the lawbreakers, Particular places to throw thrash and waste material, Public wells in every street, Well in every house, Main streets varying for 9 feet to as wide as 30-34 feet and were divided into networks of narrow lanes with great skills of dividing the cities.
 
• Building Materials-No stone-built house in the Indus cities and the staircases of big buildings were solid; the roofs were flat and were made of wood.
 
• Material used-Burnt bricks and Sun-dried bricks
 
• Drainage System-Advanced drainage and sanitation system. Each house had horizontal and vertical drains and the house drains were connected with road drains. There were underground drains for the streets and there drains were shielded by stone slabs. Bricks were used to make the soak pits.
 
• Great Granary-Great granary at Harappa measuring 169 fit x 135 fits. Attached to the granary were two-roomed tenements with a common courtyard.
 
• Great Bath-The overall dimension of the Great Public Bath is 180 feet by 108 feet. The bathing pool measured about 39 feet by 23 feet with 8 feet depth. There is a device to fill and empty the water of the bathing pool and the bathing pools were encircled with galleries and rooms.
 
• The urban planning of the Harappan has become a landmark for contemporary civilization and we can get a hint of the modern-day swimming pools and storehouses from their concept of bathing pools and granaries.
 
• Overall the Harappa town planning was very scientific and clearly indicates that the Harappan were chiefly urban people.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• Lothal(Gujarat) - It is located at the head of the Gulf of Cambay.
 
• Surkotada (Gujarat) - It is at the head of the Rann of Kutch.
 
• Banawali (Haryana) - It was situated on the banks of the now-extinct Sarasvati.
 
• Dholavira (Gujarat) - It excavated is in the Kutch district.

Social features-

 
• Indus valley civilization is the first urbanization in India.
 
• It has a well-planned drainage system, grid pattern, and town planning.
 
• They have possessed equality in society.

Religious Facts-

 
• Matridevi or Shakti is the Mother goddess.
 
• Yoni worship and Nature worship existed.
 
• They worshipped trees like Peepal.
 
• People also worshipped Fire worship called Havan Kund.
 
• Pashupati Mahadeva is known as the lord of Animals.
 
• The people of Indus Valley Civilization worshipped Animal worship like Unicorn and ox.

Economic facts-

• Trade and commerce flourished in this period.
 
• A dockyard has been found at Lothal.
 
• There were export and import.

questions.question: As per Ministry of Earth Sciences, the number of seismic observatories in India increased from 80 in 2014 to how many in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**168**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **February 2025**, the number of seismic observatories in India has increased to **168**, as per the **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)**.
 
• In **2014**, there were only **80 seismic observatories** in the country.
 
• The increase is part of the government's efforts to improve the **seismic monitoring network** across India to enhance **earthquake monitoring and disaster preparedness**.
 
• The seismic observatories are equipped with advanced technology such as **broadband seismometers** and **accelerometers** to detect and record seismic activities with high precision.
 
• The expansion aligns with India's commitment to strengthening the **National Centre for Seismology (NCS)**, which is the nodal agency for earthquake monitoring in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Centre for Seismology (NCS):**

 
 
• The **NCS** operates under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences** and is responsible for monitoring seismic activity across India.
 
• NCS provides real-time earthquake information to various stakeholders, including disaster management authorities, to ensure timely mitigation efforts.
 
• The center also conducts seismic microzonation studies to assess earthquake risks in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Seismic Observatories:**
 
 
• Seismic observatories play a crucial role in detecting **earthquakes** and studying the **tectonic movements** of the Earth's crust.
 
• They contribute to the development of **earthquake-resistant infrastructure** by providing critical data for seismic zoning and building codes.
 
• They aid in creating **early warning systems** to minimize the impact of earthquakes on human life and property.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Activity in India:**
 
 
• India is divided into **four seismic zones** (Zone II, III, IV, and V) based on the level of seismic hazard.
 
• The northeastern region, the Himalayan belt, and parts of Gujarat and Maharashtra are highly seismically active areas.
 
• The **2001 Bhuj earthquake** and the **2015 Nepal earthquake** highlighted the need for a robust seismic monitoring system.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements in Seismology:**
 
 
• Modern seismic observatories use **real-time seismic data transmission** for quicker analysis and response.
 
• Technologies like **GPS-based crustal deformation monitoring** are being integrated to study tectonic plate movements.
 
• Advancements in **machine learning** and **artificial intelligence** are being used to improve earthquake prediction models.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seismic Zoning:**

 
 
• India's seismic zones range from **Zone II** (low risk) to **Zone V** (very high risk).
 
• Seismic zoning maps are used to guide **urban planning** and **construction standards**.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake Magnitude and Intensity:**
 
 
• The **Richter scale** measures the energy released during an earthquake, while the **Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale** assesses the earthquake's impact on people and structures.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** has guidelines for earthquake preparedness and mitigation.
 
• The **Building Materials and Technology Promotion Council (BMTPC)** publishes seismic zone maps for safer construction practices.

questions.question: Who is called the father of civil services in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Lord Cornwallis__**.

__
 
• **During the British** raj, **Warren Hastings** laid the **foundation of the Civil Services.**
 
• **Charles Cornwallis reformed, modernized and rationalized it.** Hence, **Charles Cornwallis is known as 'the Father of civil service in India'.**
 
• British General Charles **Cornwallis **was appointed in **February 1786** to serve as both **Commander-in-Chief of British India **and **Governor of the Presidency of Fort William,** also known as the **Bengal Presidency**.
 
• **He had introduced** the **Covenanted Civil Services** and the **Uncovenanted Civil Services.**
 
• **The Covenanted Civil Services **was created** out of the Law of the Company.**
